## Hermes
- Loads from a plugin directory carrying `plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py`. Two verified paths (hermes_cli/plugins.py): local dev — copy this directory to `~/.hermes/plugins/docs/` (user plugin) or `./.hermes/plugins/docs/` with `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` (project plugin, opt-in) — then `hermes plugins list` should show it; from a Git host — `hermes plugins install owner/repo`, then `hermes plugins enable docs` (or pass `--enable` to `install`) to activate it — install alone does not enable a plugin. Hermes has no marketplace file, so there is no registry listing step beyond the two paths above.
- Plugin skills are NOT surfaced in `<available_skills>` (hermes_cli/plugins.py:3334-3337) — they resolve only as an explicit `<plugin>:<skill>` load. Verify with a load, e.g. `load docs:agent-harness-rules`, never with "list your skills".
- MCP: none shipped.
- Dropped — agents: `doc-checker`, `experiment-runner`, `intake-leader`, `research-leader`; hooks: none.
- Command-only skills now model-routable: `bind-intake`, `tidy-docs` (R-5, #888: `ctx.register_command` carries no invocation-source metadata on Hermes — the plain-skill degradation is the CORRECT terminal fallback here, not a temporary gap).
- Fork skills (their `context` field drops; body runs inline): `file-bug`, `file-feature`, `file-task`.

## Pi
- Loads via `package.json`'s `"pi"` key (`"skills": ["./skills"]`); install with `pi install <path-to-docs> -l` from a checkout — confirm with `pi list`, which shows the install path under `Project packages:`. The `"pi-package"` keyword is added automatically (no extra step); once this package is published, that keyword is what the pi.dev gallery scrapes to list it — there is no separate marketplace file to maintain.
- Dropped — agents: `doc-checker`, `experiment-runner`, `intake-leader`, `research-leader`; hooks: none.
- Command-only skills emitted as `prompts/{name}.md` templates (R-5 amendment, #888): `bind-intake`, `tidy-docs` — the human-only guard is preserved natively (a prompt template expands only from a human keystroke; the model has no channel to self-invoke it), unlike Codex/Hermes where these become plain, model-routable skills.
- Fork skills (their `context` field drops; body runs inline): `file-bug`, `file-feature`, `file-task`.
- MCP: none shipped.
